title: Notable recent biology and biomedical papers — arXiv announcement batch, 4 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance-ranked selection from incomplete biomedical coverage, not a readership ranking or comprehensive view of biology and medicine. Computational, simulated, retrospective, and experimental evidence are distinguished.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Latest available batch: 4 November 2026; eight papers selected. Protein design and conformational modelling dominate, alongside a DNA-model benchmark, regulatory-network software, and early intraoperative imaging. Attention evidence is sparse, so entries are ranked by relevance and evidence type, not popularity.

sections.title: ProteoCraft: Protein Design as Proposal-Verification Search
sections.abstract: ProteoCraft uses tree search guided by approximate structure-prediction gradients to propose protein sequences and separately verifies candidates with stricter structure-based scoring.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved design quality across 14 settings and prospective binding experiments: an 82.9% PD-L1 miniprotein hit rate, best measured KD 0.879 nM, and binding of a designed IFNAR2 VHH.
sections.unique_caveat: Experimental results cover selected targets and designs; broad performance, specificity, and therapeutic utility are not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct protein-interaction design relevance, three-category cross-listing, and author-reported prospective binding measurements; indexed Semantic Scholar record had 0 current citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
sections.abstract: iGC combines a learned somatic-hypermutation prior with reinforcement learning to propose antigen-specific antibody sequence changes while penalizing reward exploitation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that the learned mutation prior more than doubled the strongest baseline on mutation-site prediction and that optimization retained sequence patterns associated with SHM.
sections.unique_caveat: Generated candidates were evaluated using DMS-derived rewards rather than direct experimental measurements; wet-lab affinity improvement is not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct antibody-maturation relevance, biomolecules/ML cross-listing, and evaluations of mutation prediction, SHM consistency, reward, and diversity.

sections.title: Predicting protein structures at any folding stage from sequence
sections.abstract: FoldScape generates sequence-conditioned Cα conformational ensembles at specified folding fractions, aiming to represent intermediate as well as near-native states.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report broader folding-coordinate coverage than seed-varied AlphaFold 3 ensembles on 20 human proteins at matched sample size, while AlphaFold 3 better covers the immediate native vicinity.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes single trajectories for some protein-speed conditions and calls for more protein coverage and replicate trajectories; intermediate-state properties are not experimentally validated across the full set.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct protein-structure relevance, biomolecules/AI cross-listing, and a 20-protein comparison with an explicit baseline.

sections.title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
sections.abstract: EB-FM learns a generative prior over protein conformations directly from noisy observations using an empirical-Bayes flow-matching procedure.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report recovery of continuous conformational distributions from simulated cryo-EM observations without pretraining on clean structures.
sections.unique_caveat: Experiments assume known poses, underestimate conformational spread, and remain computationally expensive; real data with unknown poses are future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Molecular-imaging relevance and biomolecules/ML cross-listing; evaluated on controlled inverse problems and simulated cryo-EM. arXiv comment reports NeurIPS 2026 acceptance; indexed Semantic Scholar record had 0 current citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes
sections.abstract: The authors ablate protein-ensemble model and training choices across ordered, disordered, multidomain, and transitional proteins, comparing outputs against SAXS and NMR chemical-shift data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that training-source choices affected agreement more than several architecture choices; fragment-assembled ensembles improve chemical-shift agreement with a SAXS trade-off.
sections.unique_caveat: Agreement on selected observables does not establish recovery of all biological states or dynamics.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Biomolecules/ML cross-listing and comparisons to experimental SAXS and NMR across multiple structural regimes.

sections.title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
sections.abstract: BEND 2.0 evaluates genomic models on predicting DNA-change effects and guiding sequence design across eight tasks built from five experimental datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that frozen-representation linear readouts can match or exceed native model outputs, while post-training improves some capabilities; context-specific and combined-mutation effects remain harder.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective benchmark performance does not demonstrate successful prospective DNA design; context-specific and multi-cell objectives remain unsaturated.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct genomics focus, three-category cross-listing, and an eight-task/five-dataset benchmark with cross-assay and gene-transfer tests.

sections.title: GINsim 3.1: Qualitative modelling and dynamical analysis of logical regulatory networks
sections.abstract: GINsim 3.1 adds symbolic trap-space computation, Booleanisation and dynamics reversal, and extends reachability and model-reduction analyses for qualitative regulatory networks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report new qualitative analyses and CoLoMoTo interoperability, illustrated on a multilevel mammalian cell-cycle regulatory model; the software is GPL-3.0.
sections.unique_caveat: The illustration is model-based and depends on the supplied network and qualitative assumptions; it does not experimentally confirm cell-cycle mechanisms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct q-bio.MN software contribution and illustrative cell-cycle model; indexed Semantic Scholar record had 0 current citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Perioperative shear wave elastography for the evaluation of spinal cord release in pediatric dysraphism: first experience in 21 patients
sections.abstract: This retrospective, single-centre feasibility study measured spinal-cord stiffness before and after detethering surgery in 21 pediatric patients using intraoperative shear-wave elastography.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a significant pre/post stiffness decrease (25.2 to 11.2 kPa; p=0.018) and describe measurement as feasible in this cohort.
sections.unique_caveat: Single-centre retrospective data from 21 patients; no established pediatric reference values and limited clinical interpretability. The study does not show improved surgical outcomes or support practice recommendations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Human feasibility cohort with a reported sample size and analyzability endpoint; the arXiv record cites a 2026 Journal of Neurosurgery: Spine article.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Protein sequence-to-structure design and conformational sampling recur across ProteoCraft, iGC, FoldScape, EB-FM, and the protein-ensemble ablation study, with evidence ranging from computational scoring to reported binding experiments. BEND 2.0 and the protein-ensemble study examine generalization across biological contexts. The elastography cohort is a feasibility study whose authors note that missing pediatric reference values limit interpretation.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Test protein binders in blinded, prospective comparisons across targets and report expression, binding, specificity, and developability; synthesize iGC candidates and compare measured binding with DMS rewards. For FoldScape and EB-FM, add replicate trajectories, broader protein coverage, real cryo-EM data with unknown poses, and independent structural measurements. For BEND 2.0, test paired and combinatorial edits in held-out genes and matched cellular contexts. For elastography, conduct multicentre repeatability work, age-stratified reference measurements, and blinded associations with independent surgical outcomes before inferring clinical utility.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Protein design and conformational ensembles dominate this batch, with a DNA-design benchmark and early intraoperative imaging study broadening the scope. Only some papers report experiments; the clinical imaging result remains cohort-limited. This is a relevance-ranked snapshot, not a measured popularity chart.
